meta.title: Nurse Jill's First-Aid Booklet
meta.textType: functional: a booklet with a contents page and safety tips

paragraphs: On Thursday, November nineteenth, Nurse Jill came to the club hour in the school library. She carried a green first-aid kit and some small booklets. "The Explorers are going to the nature park on November twenty-eighth," she said. "This booklet is about your health on the trail." Lily, Mia, Leo, May, and Teacher Kim each took a booklet. The title was "Stay Safe on the Trail."

"Would you open the booklet at the contents page?" asked Nurse Jill. The page showed five parts, and each part had a page number. Cuts and scrapes were on page two, and insect bites were on page four. Sunburn was on page six, and hot days were on page eight. The last part, "When to ask an adult," was on page ten. "Which page has insect bites?" asked Leo. "Page four," said May. "A contents page is useful," said Nurse Jill. "You find the right part fast, because it has the page numbers."

Then Nurse Jill showed them how to look after a small cut. "First, wash the cut with clean water," she said. "Then cover it with a clean bandage." "Would you hold out your hand, Leo?" Leo held out his finger, but it had no cut. Nurse Jill put a white bandage on it. Leo smiled. "Now I am ready for the trip," he said. Everybody laughed. "Thank you," said Nurse Jill, "but please take it off later."

Page six of the booklet said, "Wear a hat on a hot day." It also said, "Put cream on your arms." "If you feel too hot, sit in a cool place and drink water," said Nurse Jill. "If an insect bites you, don't touch the bite." "Wash it with clean water instead." "Medicine from the pharmacy is for adults to give." "If a cut is big, ask an adult for advice." "This advice is very helpful," said Teacher Kim.

"Is everyone alright?" asked Nurse Jill. "Yes, thank you," said Lily. "This booklet is useful," said Mia, "so I will keep it in my bag." "Would you write your names on the booklets?" asked Nurse Jill. The children wrote their names. Leo showed his bandage to May. Lily put her booklet next to her notebook for the trip.
